pages.text: "Why are my stripes like this?" Moya peered into a rain puddle. One forehead stripe was crooked and wiggly. "I wish mine were straight like everyone else's."
Zebras passed in a line, straight stripes across their backs. Nia asked, "What's wrong?" "Everyone else's are straight. Only mine wiggles." Moya's shoulders sank.
Moya rolled in a mud puddle and covered their forehead. "Now nobody can see the wiggly stripe." Muddy Moya lowered their head sadly.
Mom touched Moya's forehead with her muzzle. "Why all the mud?" Moya sniffled and told her. "Only my stripe is crooked." Mom gently drew Moya against her side.
Mom looked at the herd. "All those zebras have black-and-white stripes, don't they?" Moya nodded. "Then how do I find you among them?"

"Your wiggly forehead stripe! I can spot it far away and know: there's my Moya! Straight stripes could belong to anyone. That wiggly one is yours alone." Moya pressed their forehead to her muzzle. "Moya is Moya!"
Nia lowered their neck to show its pattern. "Mine's special, too. That's how my mom finds me." Every brown patch was different. Moya grinned. "Nia is Nia, and Moya is Moya!"
Moya splashed into the waterhole to wash off the mud. The wiggly stripe showed clearly again. They stretched their neck and lifted their forehead. "See? That's me!"
Now Moya felt happy even in the herd. "One, look at my stripes! Two, find what's special to me! Three, shout: Moya is Moya!" Far away, Mom called at once. "There's my Moya!"
That evening, Mom cuddled and nuzzled Moya. "My one-and-only wiggly-striped Moya!" Being different helped Mom find them. Moya is Moya!
